title: Sanctification
definition: Sanctification is God's ongoing work of making believers holy and conforming them to the likeness of Jesus Christ.
summary: Sanctification is the process by which God grows believers in holiness and Christlike character.
christFocus: Jesus sanctifies His people by His Word, Spirit, and grace, forming them into His likeness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sanctification is the ongoing work of God in believers. Those whom God saves, He also changes. Sanctification involves putting off sin, renewing the mind, walking by the Spirit, and growing in love, holiness, endurance, and obedience.

This growth is not instant perfection. Believers still battle sin and weakness, but God faithfully continues His work. The Christian life is a real process of transformation.

Sanctification is rooted in union with Christ. Believers grow not to earn salvation, but because they belong to the Savior who is making them holy.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people become discouraged when change is slow or when old struggles remain. Sanctification matters because it gives realistic hope: growth may be progressive, but God is truly at work.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Cooperate with God's sanctifying work through repentance, Scripture, prayer, fellowship, accountability, and obedience. Do not confuse slow growth with no growth, and do not use grace as an excuse for sin.
